business_problem: myPOS needed to replace an increasingly rigid Microsoft SQL payment stack that was causing authorization delays, replication limits, and resilience concerns as transaction volume and merchant reach grew rapidly.
solution_summary: myPOS redesigned its payment platform around MongoDB Enterprise Advanced to support instant transaction processing, real-time fraud and security checks, and aggressive transaction growth without the limits of its previous SQL architecture. After benchmarking MongoDB against technologies such as PostgreSQL and Cassandra, the team chose an on-premises MongoDB deployment in its own data centers so it could keep latency in single-digit milliseconds while replicating reliably across two sites. Engineers did more than lift and shift: they rebuilt core acquiring, issuing, and mobile-payment services on the document model, then rolled the new architecture out in phases starting in late 2024 to avoid production disruption. MongoDB now underpins the instant-settlement experience merchants see at the edge while giving developers a more flexible schema, faster prototyping, and the capacity to scale transaction throughput as volumes rise toward a tenfold growth target.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Enterprise Advanced
solution_components.role: Runs myPOS’s core payment-processing, settlement, and real-time security workloads inside the company’s own data centers.

data_flow: Terminal, mobile, and online payment events flow into MongoDB Enterprise Advanced, where payment processing, settlement logic, and real-time security checks run with low-latency replication across myPOS’s data centers before results are returned to merchants and customers.
business_outcome: myPOS increased payment throughput dramatically, improved uptime, reduced maintenance windows, and built a scalable foundation for serving more merchants with faster and more reliable payment experiences.
